{{Short description|Mathematical relation inside orderings}}
{{For-text|other uses of "Cover" in mathematics|[[Cover (disambiguation)#Mathematics|Cover (mathematics)]]}}

[[Image:Hasse diagram of powerset of 3.svg|thumb|right|300px|The [[Hasse diagram]] of the [[power set]] of three elements, [[Partial order|partially ordered]] by [[Inclusion (set theory)|inclusion]].]]

In [[mathematics]], especially [[order theory]], the '''covering relation''' of a [[partially ordered set]] is the [[binary relation]] which holds between [[comparability|comparable]] elements that are immediate neighbours. The covering relation is commonly used to graphically express the partial order by means of the [[Hasse diagram]].

== Definition ==
Let <math>X</math> be a set with a partial order <math>\le</math>.
As usual, let <math><</math> be the relation on <math>X</math> such that <math>x<y</math> if and only if <math>x\le y</math> and <math>x\neq y</math>.

Let <math>x</math> and <math>y</math> be elements of <math>X</math>.

Then <math>y</math> '''covers''' <math>x</math>, written <math>x\lessdot y</math>,
if <math>x<y</math> and there is no element <math>z</math> such that <math>x<z<y</math>. Equivalently, <math>y</math> covers <math>x</math> if the [[partially ordered set#Intervals|interval]] <math>[x,y]</math> is the two-element set <math>\{x,y\}</math>. In more intuitive words, <math>x\lessdot y</math> if <math>y</math> immediately supersedes or succeeds <math>x</math> in terms of their respective poset's order relation.

When <math>x\lessdot y</math>, it is said that <math>y</math> is a cover of <math>x</math>. Some authors also use the term cover to denote any such pair <math>(x,y)</math> in the covering relation.

== Examples ==
* In a finite [[linearly ordered]] set <math>\{1, 2, ..., n\}</math>, <math>i+1</math> covers <math>i</math> for all <math>i</math> between <math>1</math> and <math>n-1</math>, and there are no other covering relations.
* In the [[Boolean algebra (structure)|Boolean algebra]] of the [[power set]] of a set ''S'', a subset ''B'' of ''S'' covers a subset ''A'' of ''S'' if and only if ''B'' is obtained from ''A'' by adding one element not in ''A''.
* In [[Young's lattice]], formed by the [[partition (number theory)|partitions]] of all nonnegative integers, a partition ''λ'' covers a partition ''μ'' if and only if the [[Young diagram]] of ''λ'' is obtained from the Young diagram of ''μ'' by adding an extra cell.
* The Hasse diagram depicting the covering relation of a [[Tamari lattice]] is the [[n-skeleton|skeleton]] of an [[associahedron]].
* The covering relation of any finite [[distributive lattice]] forms a [[median graph]].
* On the [[real number]]s with the usual total order ≤, no number covers another. Any such partial order in which the covering relation is empty is called "[[dense order|dense]]."

== Properties ==
* If a partially ordered set is finite, its covering relation is the [[transitive reduction]] of the partial order relation.  Such partially ordered sets are therefore completely described by their Hasse diagrams.  On the other hand, in a [[dense order]], such as the [[rational number]]s with the standard order, no element covers another.
